RAJESH RAI K. J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This Miscellaneous First Appeal is filed against the judgment dated 08.04.2019 passed in MVC No.1050/2016 by the IV-Additional District and Sessions Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.XIII, Vijayapura, wherein the Tribunal has dismissed the claim petition filed by the claimants/appellants under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act (for short, hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act').
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.
3.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal No.XIII, Vijayapura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Brief facts giving rise to filing of this appeal are that on 17.04.2016 at about 5.00 p.m., while the deceased - Sona Bai was traveling in Cruiser Station Wagon coming towards Gaddanakeri Cross from Kaladaga side, a motor car bearing registration No.AP-02-AE-1724 came from opposite direction and dashed against the vehicle in which the deceased was traveling.

As a result, NC:
2024:KHC-K:3863-DB the deceased-Sona Bai sustained injuries and was shifted to Kerudi Hospital,
Bagalkot and she was treated as inpatient for 14 days and thereafter, she was discharged.

However,
after discharge from the hospital, she succumbed to the injuries.
As such, legal heirs of the deceased-Sona Bai filed claim petition before the Tribunal seeking compensation stating that the death of Sona Bai was caused due to the accident dated 17.04.2016.
4. After service of notice to the respondents, the respondents have resisted the claim petition filed by the petitioners by filing statement of objections.
5. The Tribunal after considering the claim petition so also statement of objections, framed the relevant issues for its consideration.

6. In order to prove the claim petition before the Tribunal, claimant No.1 examined himself as PW.1 and two other witnesses were examined as PWs.2 and 3 so also got marked 08 documents as Exs.P1 to P8.

However, the NC: 2024:KHC-K:3863-DB respondent-Insurance Companies have not examined any witnesses on their behalf however, got marked one document as Ex.R1.
7.
After assessment of oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal dismissed the claim petition filed by the claimants.
8. Aggrieved by the impugned judgment passed by the Tribunal, the claimants have filed this appeal before this Court.

sentences.text: We have heard the learned counsel for the appellants and learned counsel for respondents Nos.2 and 4, Insurance Companies.

10. It is the primary contention of the learned counsel for the appellants that the Tribunal erred while dismissing the claim petition without considering the evidence of PWs.1 to 3, so also documents placed before it.
The death of the deceased is not in dispute that the same was caused due to road traffic accident.
In such NC: 2024:KHC-K:3863-DB circumstance, the Tribunal ought to have allowed the claim petition filed by the petitioners.

He would further contend that though charge sheet Ex.P6 filed by the police reveals that the charge sheet laid against the driver of the car in which the petitioner was traveling, itself will not be a ground to dismiss the claim petition.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the claim petition.
11. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company supported the impugned judgment and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.

12. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and having considered the documents made available before us, the point that arises for our consideration is:
1. Whether the Tribunal is justified in rejecting the claim petition filed by the claimants?
13. As could be seen from the records, the just and proper have investigated the case in respect of the alleged NC: 2024:KHC-K:3863-DB accident in which the deceased died.
On perusal of Ex.P3, the spot mahazar, depicts that the accident was caused in the middle of the road.
Further on inspection of the motor vehicles by the inspector, he ruled out the mechanical failure of the vehicle.

As such,
the charge sheet has been laid against the driver of the car i.e., car bearing registration No.AP-02/AE-1724.
hence, it is clear that the driver of the said car was the author of accident.
As such, the claim petition by the claimants against the respondent-Insurance Company does not holds good.
There is no such rebuttal evidence placed by the appellants before the Tribunal to substantiate their claim.
Further, though the claimants have placed pathology report and wound certificate, they failed to produce single medical bill to honour the medical claim.
The petitioners have also failed to produce the post mortem report to substantiate their claim that the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident and the deceased died due to the same.
In such circumstance, in our considered view, the Tribunal is justified in rejecting the claim petition.
With the above discussions, we are of the considered opinion that the Tribunal has rightly rejected the claim petition and there is no good ground to interfere with the order passed by the Tribunal.

15. Accordingly, we answer the point raised above in the negative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The appeal is dismissed as being devoid of merits.
